verdict.reasoning: Patient states: "I've been having, uh, diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days, more or less."
When asked frequency and character: "Yeah, around, five to six times a day" and "Yes, it's definitely, definitely watery, uh, loose stools, yeah."

Patient: "so it started with vomiting, so I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away, and, uh, yeah it's just diarrhoea now." This supports initial vomiting episodes that resolved; "couple of times" ≈ twice.
Doctor: "Any blood in your stools?" Patient: "No, not that I could see."
Doctor: "with the diarrhea have you noticed any other symptoms, like tummy pain?" Patient: "Uh, not, not really, no."
Patient: "probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel, I feel kind of fine."
Patient: "I feel very dehydrated" and later "I feel very weak though."
Patient: "have you managed to eat anything, solids?" – "Uh, not much, not much. So just a little bit, but I don't feel, um, I don't really feel like, uh, I have appetite."
Doctor: "Any headaches or muscle pains?" Patient: "Not, not really, no."
Patient: "I, I do suffer of asthma."
Patient: "So, I do have my inhalers, uh, that I... I use infrequently" and confirms it is the blue inhaler when doctor asks: "Is that the blue inhaler?" Patient: "Yes it is, yeah."
Doctor: "Do you have any allergies to medications?" Patient: "Um, not that I know of."
Patient: "my father has, high uh, well used to have high blood pressure. He actually, so he actually died, of, bowel cancer, like ten years ago."
Regarding mother: Patient: "she has diabetes." Doctor: "Do you know if that's type one or type two?" Patient: "Uh, it's type two."
Living situation: Doctor: "Who lives at home with you, sir?" Patient: "Ohh I, I live alone." Employment: Doctor: "What do you do for work?" Patient: "I'm a software engineer."
Doctor: "Have you taken time off work recently?" Patient: "Uh, yes, yes I have, uh. Uh, these last three days I've been feeling, really unwell, so I couldn't work."
Doctor: "regarding your smoking and alcohol. Do you do either of those?" Patient: "... I don't smoke."
Same exchange: Patient: "not really, I drink infrequently, like socially let's say" describing alcohol use.

Doctor: "I think you're probably suffering from what we call gastroenteritis" and earlier patient reports "diarrhoea, for like, let's say past three days" with watery stools; together support acute gastroenteritis with 3‑day watery diarrhea.
Doctor confirms: "the vomiting has now stopped. Is that right?" Patient: "Yes, yes." and earlier "I vomited a couple of times. Uh, but then, that went away, and, uh, yeah it's just diarrhoea now."
No blood: Patient: "No, not that I could see" to blood in stools. No abdominal pain: Patient: "Uh, not, not really, no" when asked about tummy pain.

Feverish early: "probably at, at the beginning I was feeling I had a bit of temperature, but now I feel, I feel kind of fine." Weak and low intake: "I feel very weak though" and "not much, not much" solids with poor appetite.

No clear trigger: Patient does not recall any specific precipitant and denies suspect food ("not that I remember" to takeaway) and sick contacts ("Hmm, not that I know"). This supports no clear exposure.
Asthma: "I do suffer of asthma" and "I do have my inhalers... I use infrequently" indicating stable asthma with infrequent inhaler use.

Doctor: "you can drink plenty of fluids" and "you can get things from the pharmacy, which is called Dioralyte, which can help replenish any uh minerals and vitamins you may have lost... a type of fluid replacement drink."
Doctor: "you can take some Paracetamol if you're feeling feverish and weak."
Doctor: "I would probably advise you to continue taking time off work for next day or two, until you get better."
Doctor: "normally you have to be diarrhea-free for about twenty four to forty eight hours, before you return back to work."
The transcript notes asthma and inhaler use but contains no advice such as "Continue using the inhaler as needed for asthma." This specific plan instruction is not stated.
Doctor: "Let's see how the next few days go. And if you're still not better next week, I want you to come back and see me."
